case_name: Ghulam Rasool Lone v State of Jammu and Kashmir and Another
respondent:
State of Jammu and Kashmir and Another
Supreme Court of India

16 July 2009
SLP (Civil) No. 14126 of 2009
The Judgment was delivered by : S. B. Sinha, J.
1.  One Hamiddulah Dar was an Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police. He was granted promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector illegally upon relaxing the prescribed Rules in the year 1987. Seven persons said to be similarly situated asked for similar treatment.
2.  SWP No.519 of 1987 was filed by one of them, named Abdul Rashid Rather, a Constable. It was allowed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court by an order dated 24th September, 1998. A Letters Patent Appeal filed thereagainst was dismissed by a Division Bench of the High Court by its order dated 30th July, 1999. It is stated that a Special Leave Petition filed against the said order was also dismissed by this Court.
3.  Another writ petition was filed by four persons, namely - Maharaj Krishan Bhatt 2008 Indlaw SC 1206, Mohammad Amin, Bansilal Bhatt and Mohamm
facts: One Hamiddulah Dar was an Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police.
He was granted promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector illegally upon relaxing the prescribed Rules in the year 1987.
Seven persons said to be similarly situated asked for similar treatment.
SWP No.519 of 1987 was filed by one of them, named Abdul Rashid Rather, a Constable.
It was allowed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court by an order dated 24th September, 1998.
A Letters Patent Appeal filed thereagainst was dismissed by a Division Bench of the High Court by its order dated 30th July, 1999.

Another writ petition was filed by four persons in the year 1997, which was registered as SWP No.3735 of 1997, praying for their promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector with effect from the date on which Hamiddulah Dar, who was said to be junior to the petitioners, was promoted.
A learned Single Judge of the High Court allowed the said writ petition by an order dated 30th April, 2001.
On an intra court appeal having been preferred, a Division Bench of the said Court by its order dated 11th October, 2002 allowed the same.
issues: Was the petitioner-respondent sitting on the fence and sought to obtain success on the basis of success of another?

Was the Division Bench wrong in its approach so as to warrant interference therewith by this Court in exercise of its extra ordinary jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution of India, is the question.
petitioner_arguments: The Division Bench of the High Court committed a serious error in passing the impugned judgment in so far as it failed to take into consideration that delay or latches alone could be a ground for discriminating the petitioner vis-'-vis five others, who were similarly situated.
The promotion of said Hamidullah Dar was illegal.
respondent_arguments: He having not expressed grievance as regard special treatment meted out to Hamiddulah Dar for a long period of time, in law, cannot be permitted to leap forward for the first time, on the basis of success of another who had been pursuing his grievance right from the date when the subject unwarranted favour was shown to Hamidullah Dar.
court_reasoning: The Division Bench opined :- 'He having not expressed grievance as regard special treatment meted out to Hamiddulah Dar for a long period of time, in law, cannot be permitted to leap forward for the first time, on the basis of success of another who had been pursuing his grievance right from the date when the subject unwarranted favour was shown to Hamidullah Dar.'
The Court held: 'Article 14 of the Constitution of India has a positive concept. Equality, it is trite, cannot be claimed in illegality.'
holding: The Division Bench's approach was not wrong and this Court will not interfere with its judgment.
